refs.description: Mental health diversion — primary alternative to conviction + probation. If § 1001.36 succeeds, § 1203 never applies. Cross-reference pen_code_1001_36_mental_health_diversion.
Misdemeanor diversion — primary alternative for M25-00758. If § 1001.95 succeeds, § 1203 never applies. Cross-reference pen_code_1001_95_misdemeanor_diversion.

Expungement after successful probation completion — after completing probation, defendant may petition to withdraw plea or set aside verdict. Available for § 273d if probation is completed successfully. Post-completion relief pathway.

Victim restitution — mandatory as a condition of probation. The probation officer report must address the amount of restitution. Where the 'victim' is the false accuser, restitution may be disputed or offset by counter-claims.
Criteria affecting probation — court rules listing factors to consider in granting or denying probation. Defense sentencing memo should address each factor in rule 4.414.

Mental health treatment as condition of probation — court may impose mental health treatment as a probation condition. If diversion is unavailable, accepting a treatment condition is a pathway to reduced supervision and § 1203.4 expungement.

Violent felony list — § 1203(k) bars probation if defendant was on felony probation at time of new offense AND new offense is a violent or serious felony. Must verify defendant's current probation status.
